facts.text: Evart was named after Civil War veteran Perry "Frank" Everts, but a clerical error misspelled his name as Evart when the post office opened in 1870.
The town grew around timber, with the first sawmill built in 1851 by James Kennedy, making Evart a key sorting point for lumber floated down the Muskegon River.
In 1990 the Evart Glass Plant, originally built by Chrysler for automotive glass, moved there, boosting manufacturing after the lumber era.
Evart was incorporated as a city on March 4, 1930, gaining home‑rule authority during a period of economic transition.
The Evart Downtown Historic District was added to the National Register of Historic Places on August 11, 2025, the county’s only listing.
Delos Blodgett and James Stimson settled the area that became Evart in 1850, arriving by canoe along the Muskegon River and starting a lumber camp the next year.
